note: Does proportional extraction behave like simply reducing the die power? Re-measured 27 Aug 2026 on the CORRECTED --spreading boundary at the settled 200 um burial depth, because the handbook's version of this check was made on the superseded boundary at 100 um burial. The prediction is a separate no-cooling solve of the same stack at (1-f) of the die power; the measurement is the proportional strategy removing f.
driver: examples/die_average_cooling.py --die-W {97,90,70} (prediction) vs the proportional arm of die_average_strategies.json
result: The claim STANDS and is STRENGTHENED. Removing a fraction f of the heat where it is made moves the peak almost exactly as if the die dissipated (1-f) of its power, with a residual that grows with f: +0.27 K at 3 W, +0.92 K at 10 W, +2.76 K at 30 W.
why_this_is_stronger_than_a_restatement: The residuals are IDENTICAL to two decimal places to those measured on the superseded boundary (+0.27 / +0.92 / +2.76), even though that boundary differed by a factor of 4.25 in K/W and the burial depth was half. The residual is therefore a property of the ARRAY LAYER -- its own thermal resistance and the silicon buried beneath it -- and not of the sink. A number that reproduces across a boundary change of that size is evidence about the mechanism, not a coincidence of calibration.
caveat: These are linear solves with no leakage feedback, by design: the question is whether the geometry behaves like a power reduction, and leakage feedback would confound that with its own temperature dependence. It is not a statement about behaviour near the runaway cliff, where feedback dominates.
